# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Taylor Jennings**
[Street address]
[City], HI [ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** 'Ohana Health Plan — Appeals and Grievances
[Appeal address exactly as printed on my denial letter]

**RE:** Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-15
**Member:** Taylor Jennings
**Member ID:** W164265496
**Reference number:** POC-209DEB4204-66822
**Service denied:** Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
**Governing policy:** 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines, effective 2026-07-01 — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

---

## 1. What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization for a total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), issued by 'Ohana Health Plan on 2026-08-15 under reference number POC-209DEB4204-66822. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery. My surgeon, Marchetti, MD, requested this procedure and documented the need for it in the prior authorization packet.

The notice states that the request was denied because the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am writing because my records document a completed course of conservative treatment, and I would like that record reviewed against the plan's own written standard.

## 2. The plan's own definition of failed conservative treatment

The 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines define what it means for conservative treatment to have failed:

> "NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following:"

> "○ Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment;"

> "OR ○ Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment;"

The guidelines also state:

> "OR ○ Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute “inability to complete” treatment."

That last sentence describes the situations that do **not** count as a failed trial — missed care, inconvenience, or unexplained noncompliance. None of those apply to me. I completed the treatment that was prescribed.

## 3. How my records match that standard

| The plan's standard | What my records show |
|---|---|
| A full course of treatment, completed | Supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, 10 weeks, from 2026-04-14 to 2026-06-23, with **24 visits completed**. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. |
| Medication trial | NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief. |
| Injection trial | Corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-02, which gave 3 weeks of partial relief. |
| "Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment" | After all of the above, my exam still shows positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height, and I cannot sleep on the affected side. |
| "Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment" | My records describe **14 months of progressive pain** in the shoulder, unrelieved by rest. |
| Objective imaging | MRI of the shoulder dated 2026-06-19: full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. |
| Surgical candidacy factors | No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker. |

I did not skip conservative care. I completed 24 supervised physical therapy visits over 10 weeks, took anti-inflammatory medication for four months, and had a steroid injection that helped for three weeks. My symptoms did not meaningfully improve, and the pain has been progressive over 14 months. Under the plan's own definition, that is failure of conservative treatment.

## 4. A note about which criteria were applied

I want to be straightforward with the reviewer about one thing. The criteria excerpts available to me from the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines are the cervical fusion sections — Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion, Cervical Posterior Decompression with Fusion, and Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain. Those sections address the neck and spine. My requested surgery is a shoulder replacement. I am therefore **not** quoting a shoulder arthroplasty criterion, because no shoulder-specific criterion has been identified to me in writing. Everything I have said above about my shoulder is in my own words and drawn from my medical records; the only text I have placed in quotation marks is the guidelines' definition of failed conservative treatment, which is the standard the denial reason turns on.

## 5. Request for the criteria that were actually applied

**I am formally requesting, in writing, a copy of the specific clinical criteria used to deny this request** — the exact policy title, section, and criterion language the reviewer applied to CPT 23472, along with the name and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination. The plan and its review vendor hold those criteria; I do not. My plan uses Evolent for musculoskeletal surgery review, and Evolent publishes its guidelines publicly at the link above, with no login required. If a different section or a different document was used, I ask that it be sent to me so that I can respond to the actual standard my records were measured against.

## 6. Closing request

I respectfully ask 'Ohana Health Plan to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-15 and authorize the total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472) requested by Marchetti, MD. My records document a completed, supervised, and unsuccessful course of conservative treatment that meets the definition of failed conservative treatment set out in the plan's own guidelines, along with objective MRI findings and continued functional loss.

If any additional records would help — the physical therapy discharge note, the injection record, the MRI report, or the surgeon's office notes — please tell me what is needed and I will have them sent promptly. I also ask to be told how to request an external review if this appeal is not approved.

**Appeal deadline and submission.** My denial notice states that this appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date, by **2027-02-11**. I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also file online at ambetterhealth.com by selecting my state (Hawaii) and using that state's appeal or grievance form, or by calling the number on my member ID card. The address and instructions on my denial letter are the ones I am following.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this.

Sincerely,

**Taylor Jennings**
Member ID: W164265496
Reference number: POC-209DEB4204-66822
[Signature]
[Date signed]

**Enclosures:** [List what you enclose — e.g., physical therapy discharge note dated 2026-06-23; MRI report dated 2026-06-19; injection record dated 2026-04-02; office notes from Marchetti, MD; copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-15]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
